name: Save the Cat (15-beat sheet)
license_note: Beat names are widely-taught structural vocabulary; prompts are original prose. No Snyder text is reproduced.

beats.name: Opening Image
beats.prompt: What single image states the 'before' world?

beats.name: Theme Stated
beats.prompt: Who voices the lesson the protagonist must learn, and how obliquely?

beats.name: Set-Up
beats.prompt: Which flaws, wants and stakes must the reader see before everything changes?

beats.name: Catalyst
beats.prompt: What event makes the old life impossible to continue?

beats.name: Debate
beats.prompt: What question does the protagonist wrestle with before committing?

beats.name: Break into Two
beats.prompt: What choice moves the protagonist into the new world?

beats.name: B Story
beats.prompt: Which relationship carries the theme while the A-plot runs?

beats.name: Fun and Games
beats.prompt: What is the promise of the premise — the scenes on the poster?

beats.name: Midpoint
beats.prompt: What false victory or false defeat raises the stakes and starts the clock?

beats.name: Bad Guys Close In
beats.prompt: How do external pressure and internal dissent tighten together?

beats.name: All Is Lost
beats.prompt: What loss (with a whiff of death) strips the protagonist bare?

beats.name: Dark Night of the Soul
beats.prompt: What does the protagonist finally understand in the wreckage?

beats.name: Break into Three
beats.prompt: How do A-story and B-story fuse into the solution?

beats.name: Finale
beats.prompt: How is the lesson proven in action, step by step?

beats.name: Final Image
beats.prompt: What closing image mirrors the opening and shows the change?
